assumptions: The founder can conduct direct outbound and build the workflow using only independently obtained, non-confidential resources.
Target customers can legally authorize the business to process their evidence and route supplier requests under appropriately reviewed agreements.
The founder enforces portfolio and request limits and uses qualified counsel or customer experts for regulatory conclusions.
The managed service is offered only after a paid baseline demonstrates sufficient recurring exception volume and buyer value.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Multiple paid baselines from a tightly defined segment, signed workflow and data-processing agreements, observed baseline-to-managed conversion, measured CAC and sales cycle, account-level labor and fully loaded contribution margin, resolution-time or avoided-cost improvement, quarterly renewal, and evidence that delivery can be delegated without quality loss would support higher scores.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The redesign recognizes that accountable collection and exception closure may be more valuable than generic document storage, and makes customer authorization the route into the workflow. This is a sounder wedge, though consultants and platforms can reproduce the service.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Regulatory documentation duties, observed buyer-side supplier requests, and public paid PPWR offerings support a credible problem and budget category. The fixed baseline ties payment to a concrete gap, but no buyer has purchased this specific baseline or managed term and portfolio-level urgency remains uneven.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Prepaid setup, quarterly advance billing, explicit work allowances, excess-work charges, and pilot-level time tracking improve cash conversion and downside control. The 45-65% contribution-margin target, direct CAC, conversion, capacity, retention, owner earnings, and 5M PLN path remain unvalidated, while labor intensity limits operating leverage.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Mid-market brands with dated evidence gaps, approval backlogs, or supplier changes are a clearer beachhead than the original broad vault market. It is still not narrowed by geography, packaging category, obligation, or portfolio profile, and the number of buyers with acute gaps and no adequate alternative is unknown.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Owning the direct service relationship and operating the customer's exception queue could create workflow familiarity and switching friction within a narrow segment. The position is nonexclusive and replaceable, and PLM vendors, consultants, and low-cost tools can offer overlapping functionality, limiting domination potential.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Successful baselines can expand into recurring queue operation, additional portfolios, supplier changes, other geographies, and adjacent compliance workflows. Expansion is constrained by customer-specific rights, service labor, and unproven baseline-to-managed conversion and renewal.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Operating playbooks, exception taxonomies, integrations, and measured service performance could improve over time. The proposed agreement is unsigned, access is account-specific and revocable, cross-customer benchmarking needs separate consent, and competitors can reproduce the workflow.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: A prepaid, bounded, customer-upload fallback with accountable exception closure is more immediately actionable than buying and implementing a full platform. The magnitude of improvement in resolution time, cost, accuracy, or approval delay has not been demonstrated against software, internal staff, or consultants.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: General PPWR application in August 2026 creates a current opening for evidence baselines and workflow remediation. Important requirements phase through 2030, so sales timing must target portfolios with present documentation duties or backlogs rather than rely on broad regulatory urgency.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Founder-controlled direct outbound removes dependence on unsigned referral partners and permits a focused, measurable launch. Nevertheless, there is no observed response rate, sales cycle, conversion, CAC, signed buyer, or evidence that part-time outbound can become repeatable and scalable.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The 55,000 PLN plan, prepaid pilots, bounded delivery, contractor use, and data-workflow fit are feasible for an initial test alongside employment. Material risks remain around customer authorization, source-document access, regulatory and professional liability, cybersecurity, contractor quality, founder capacity, and strict employer separation.

highest_value_structural_change: Narrow the launch to one packaging category and buyer profile with a present, measurable documentation backlog, then standardize a repeatable exception-closure playbook and price it against verified avoided labor or delay before attempting broader managed-service expansion.
main_structural_strength: The prepaid baseline plus customer-authorized managed workflow creates a controllable, low-capital validation path tied to a concrete buyer problem without requiring a proprietary shared dataset or referral partner at launch.
primary_score_limiter: The redesigned offer remains an unsigned, labor-intensive, replaceable service with no validated acquisition, conversion, contribution margin, renewal, or measurable advantage over internal teams, consultants, and bundled software.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Existing low-price PPWR tools and Specright already cover much of the document, supplier, approval, and reporting workflow, while no customer has yet signed the proposed workflow agreement or paid for the redesigned service.
